mechanism: Baclofen (GABA-B agonist) causes CNS depression while amphetamine causes CNS stimulation, creating opposing pharmacodynamic effects and potential for unpredictable CNS outcomes; amphetamine may also reduce baclofen's efficacy for spasticity management.
action: Concurrent use requires careful clinical monitoring; consider alternative stimulant agents or adjust baclofen dosing; monitor for reduced spasticity control and CNS effects.
